content: Paul David, CC, GOQ, MD (December 25, 1919 – April 5, 1999), was a distinguished Canadian cardiologist, the founder of the Montreal Heart Institute, and a Senator. He was born in Montreal, Quebec, to Louis-Athanase David and Antonia Nantel. He earned his Bachelor’s degree from the University of Paris in 1939 and completed his medical degree (MD) at the Université de Montréal in 1944. Dr. David pursued advanced specialization in cardiology, training at the Massachusetts General Hospital in Boston in 1946 and at the Hôpital Lariboisière in Paris in 1947. Upon returning to Montreal, he joined the staff of the Notre-Dame Hospital. In 1954, he established the Montreal Heart Institute, which became a leading center for cardiovascular care and research. Under his leadership, the first heart transplant in Canada was successfully performed at the Institute in 1968. In 1985, Dr. David was appointed to the Canadian Senate on the recommendation of Prime Minister Brian Mulroney. He served as a Progressive Conservative senator representing the senatorial division of Bedford, Quebec. He retired from the Senate on his 75th birthday in 1994. Notably, his father, Louis-Athanase David, and his grandfather, Laurent-Olivier David, had also served as Senators. Dr. David received numerous honors throughout his career. In 1968, he was appointed an Officer of the Order of Canada and was later promoted to Companion in 1981. In 1988, he was named a Grand Officer of the National Order of Quebec. He was married to Yvette Lemire, and together they had six children: Françoise, Pierre, Charles-Philippe, Thérèse, Anne-Marie, and Hélène.
